cards.title: Above-the-fold formula: value prop, image, one CTA, social proof
cards.summary: The only section every visitor sees should state what's in it for me in 5 seconds with a reinforcing image, a single obvious CTA and trust proof.
cards.use_when: Redesigning the first screen of a homepage, PDP or landing page where you must convert cold traffic.

cards.title: Build visual hierarchy so the eye knows where to go
cards.summary: Use size contrast, color contrast and separation to direct attention from headline to body to CTA.
cards.use_when: When a page looks cluttered or the headline, body and CTA compete for attention during a design review.

cards.title: Time pop-ups to intent, not arrival
cards.summary: Replace immediate pop-ups with exit-intent, post-add-to-cart or scroll-depth triggers to target visitors already ready to act.
cards.use_when: Setting pop-up triggers on a store and deciding when the discount or email capture should fire.

cards.title: Cut options: paradox of choice on bundles and navigation
cards.summary: Consolidating bundle tiers and cutting low-use navigation improves both conversion and average order value.
cards.use_when: When a PDP offers too many bundle options or the site navigation has grown past seven items.

cards.title: Strategic bundling and making savings obvious
cards.summary: Bundle complementary products at a discount and state the savings in the headline instead of burying them in body text.
cards.use_when: Structuring bundle offers on a PDP or bundle page to raise perceived value and AOV.

cards.title: Price anchoring and the middle option bias
cards.summary: Raise the 'compare at' price to inflate perceived savings, and structure tier savings so the middle bundle looks like the safest value.
cards.use_when: Setting bundle tiers, compare-at prices and savings labels on a PDP or bundle page.

cards.title: Humanize the brand to build know-like-trust
cards.summary: Team photos, behind-the-scenes content, customer success videos and conversational copy make an online store feel like a person.
cards.use_when: Building an About page, brand story or PDP copy on a store where trust is the barrier to purchase.

cards.title: Reduce FUD (fear, uncertainty, doubt) at the point of action
cards.summary: Answer the anxieties that block purchase — guarantees, security badges, shipping clarity and transparent pricing — right where the customer acts.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a cart, PDP or checkout where hesitation or drop-off suggests unresolved buyer anxiety.

cards.title: Make content scannable, not readable
cards.summary: Convert dense blocks into bullets, icons, subheadings and bold highlights because users scan rather than read.
cards.use_when: Writing or revising product descriptions, landing page copy or feature sections.

cards.title: A/B testing framework: prioritize, isolate, run long, document
cards.summary: Use impact-versus-effort prioritization, single-variable tests, a minimum two-week run and documented learnings to keep improving a landing page.
cards.use_when: Planning a CRO test roadmap for a store's landing pages and PDPs after implementing quick wins.

cards.title: Write the Advertorial for One Real Customer, Not a Crowd
cards.summary: Pick a single verified buyer from your ad data and write the advertorial as if it were for them alone, which makes it resonate with many.
cards.use_when: When briefing or drafting an advertorial, pre-lander, listicle or VSL and deciding which customer to write to.

cards.title: Audit Your Draft for the Moment the Story Stops
cards.summary: Read the advertorial back and flag every sentence where storytelling turns into a sales pitch — those are the tab-close points.
cards.use_when: When editing a finished advertorial or pre-lander before publishing, to find where narrative breaks down.

cards.title: Write the After State First, Then Work Backwards
cards.summary: Define the customer's desired future life in vivid detail first, then reverse-engineer the before-state pain so the contrast is visceral.
cards.use_when: When structuring the transformation arc of an advertorial, PDP story block, or landing page for a solution-style product.

cards.title: Use the Full Storytelling Sequence for a Pre-Lander
cards.summary: A repeatable advertorial structure: benefit headline, mirror, agitate, failed solutions, unique mechanism, social proof, transformation, soft CTA.
cards.use_when: When outlining a pre-lander or advertorial from scratch and deciding the order of sections.

cards.title: Name the Unique Mechanism So Readers Can Repeat It
cards.summary: Give the product's mechanism a scientific-sounding name and frame it so the reader feels smart enough to retell it at a party.
cards.use_when: When introducing the mechanism that explains how your product works inside an advertorial or landing page.

cards.title: Soft-Sell: Weave the Product Into the Narrative Without Breaking Story
cards.summary: Integrate the product through a character's voice (e.g. a doctor asking where to get it) instead of switching into hard-sales copy.
cards.use_when: When the advertorial needs to mention the product or where to obtain it without jarring the reader out of the story.

cards.title: Delay the Sticky CTA Until After the Product Is Introduced
cards.summary: The sticky 'Check Availability' button should only appear once the reader has scrolled past the point where the product is introduced.
cards.use_when: When implementing the sticky/scroll-triggered CTA on an advertorial or long-form landing page.

cards.title: Reinforce Copy with Photorealistic, Paragraph-Matched Images
cards.summary: Every image should visually confirm the paragraph above it, using amateur 'phone-photo' style rather than polished stock.
cards.use_when: When selecting or briefing images for an advertorial, pre-lander, or story-style landing page.

cards.title: Apply the Ad-to-Page Congruency Principle Across the Funnel
cards.summary: Carry the same persona, hook, problem and promise from ad creative into the advertorial headline and body through to the product page.
cards.use_when: When planning a paid-traffic funnel (ad → pre-lander → PDP) for a specific segment.

cards.title: Write a Benefit-Driven Advertorial Headline Template
cards.summary: Structure the headline around the exact persona, the problem, and the transformation, using the value equation, kept deliberately simple.
cards.use_when: When drafting the headline for an advertorial, pre-lander, or VSL that runs from paid traffic.

cards.title: Doubling conversion beats doubling traffic
cards.summary: Frame landing-page optimization as the higher-leverage path to revenue growth because it multiplies the return on traffic you already pay for.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to spend budget and effort when an ecommerce store already has traffic but flat sales — choosing between scaling ad spend and rebuilding the PDP/landing page.

cards.title: Win the above-the-fold section
cards.summary: Treat the top section as the highest-value real estate because 100% of visitors see it and roughly 60% never scroll past it.
cards.use_when: Designing or auditing the hero area of a landing page or product page where you need visitors to act or scroll before they leave.

cards.title: Use the 'so that' chain to find the real benefit
cards.summary: Drill a feature statement down to its ultimate customer outcome by repeatedly asking 'so that…' before writing the headline.
cards.use_when: Writing a landing-page headline, PDP benefit bullet, or ad hook when copy currently just names the product or feature.

cards.title: Match the headline to buyer awareness level
cards.summary: Pick the value-proposition framing based on how aware the traffic is of your problem and product.
cards.use_when: Writing headlines for cold paid traffic versus warm email/organic traffic landing on the same product or store.

cards.title: Stack multiple forms of social proof above the fold
cards.summary: Place several distinct credibility signals — rating badges, user counts, client logos, quantified results — in the first screen, not just one.
cards.use_when: Building the hero of a landing page or PDP where you need instant credibility before a visitor decides to scroll or buy.

cards.title: Design visual hierarchy so the CTA is obvious when blurred
cards.summary: Use font size, weight, and contrast to guide the eye from headline to CTA, testing clarity by blurring the page.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a landing page or PDP layout where the main action is unclear or competing with other elements.

cards.title: Reduce FUD directly under the conversion button
cards.summary: Place risk-reversal copy — guarantees, free trial, no credit card required — immediately beneath the CTA to move hesitant buyers over the line.
cards.use_when: Placing or reviewing a buy button, add-to-cart, or demo-booking CTA where hesitation is suppressing conversion.

cards.title: Repeat CTAs throughout the page
cards.summary: Don't rely on a single top-of-page button — scatter the same conversion action at every natural decision point so visitors can act whenever interest peaks.
cards.use_when: Laying out a long landing page or product page where the CTA appears only once at the top.

cards.title: Strip friction from the contact/conversion form
cards.summary: Simplify lead and checkout forms by trimming fields, keeping labels visible, and giving a reason to submit.
cards.use_when: Redesigning a lead form or checkout/signup step where drop-off is high or leads are low quality.

cards.title: Use progressive disclosure on lead forms
cards.summary: Ask for one simple piece of information first, then reveal additional fields after the user engages, lowering perceived effort.
cards.use_when: Designing a demo-booking or signup form where you need more data but don't want to scare users off with a long form.

cards.title: Scroll the CTA to an on-page form instead of linking away
cards.summary: Keep conversion on the same page by having the hero CTA scroll down to the form rather than navigate to a separate page.
cards.use_when: Testing whether to send interested visitors to a separate contact/checkout page versus scrolling them to an embedded form.

cards.title: Build multiple benefit-driven sections, not just one
cards.summary: Dedicate several sections purely to benefits and differentiation instead of compressing everything into one or two blocks.
cards.use_when: Structuring a long landing page or product page and deciding how much space to give to benefits versus features.

cards.title: Use the contrast principle: lead with the pain, then the solution
cards.summary: Headline around a specific pain the audience hates, then immediately resolve it, to make the value proposition land emotionally.
cards.use_when: Writing headlines or sections for a product whose main appeal is removing a hated task or avoiding a feared outcome.

cards.title: Write 'you'-focused copy throughout the page
cards.summary: Frame every headline and section around the reader's experience and outcomes, minimizing the brand as subject.
cards.use_when: Rewriting landing-page or PDP copy that reads as company-centric ('we are…', 'our product…') rather than customer-centric.

cards.title: Use a hero visual that reinforces the value proposition
cards.summary: Choose an image or video in the hero that actively demonstrates or embodies what you do, not decoration.
cards.use_when: Deciding which hero image or video to place above the fold on a landing page or PDP.

cards.title: Place targeted social proof at decision points, not just up top
cards.summary: Scatter hand-picked testimonials and proof throughout the page, each backing a specific claim or objection, especially where people drop off.
cards.use_when: Planning where testimonials, case studies, and logos should appear across a landing page or PDP funnel.

cards.title: Elicit testimonials with leading questions
cards.summary: Collect proof that maps to your page's claims by asking customers structured questions about problem, goal, and outcome.
cards.use_when: Requesting testimonials or reviews from customers so they can be used as targeted landing-page and PDP proof.

cards.title: Advertorial Definition and Credibility Transfer
cards.summary: An advertorial is a paid advertisement formatted as editorial content so readers transfer the host publication's trust to your brand.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to buy sponsored-placement content on a publisher, newsletter, or platform versus running a standard display or social ad for a product.

cards.title: The 70/30 Content-to-Pitch Ratio
cards.summary: Write advertorials as roughly 70% genuinely useful or entertaining content and 30% or less promotional pitch so people read, engage and share them.
cards.use_when: Writing any sponsored article, advertorial, paid newsletter placement, or top-of-funnel content piece intended to drive product discovery and sharing.

cards.title: AppSumo's Daily Deal Email Structure
cards.summary: AppSumo's daily deal emails to ~750,000 subscribers led with a story or how-to rather than a hard sell, keeping the promo under ~30%.
cards.use_when: Designing promotional emails or sponsored placements for a deal, bundle, or product launch to a large list where unsubscribes and low open rates are a risk.

cards.title: The Tear-Out Benchmark (Ogilvy)
cards.summary: David Ogilvy's advertorials succeeded because they were useful enough that readers physically tore them out to keep as reference.
cards.use_when: Judging whether a piece of sponsored or content-marketing material is valuable enough to earn saves, shares and repeat exposure for a product.

cards.title: Build Shareability With Listicle and Fun-Content Sponsored Posts
cards.summary: Sponsors gain reach by paying for entertaining, shareable listicles that are only loosely related to the product, not direct product ads.
cards.use_when: Planning a top-of-funnel sponsored placement on a listicle site or social platform when direct product ads get scrolled past.

cards.title: Warm Up Cold Audiences Before the Direct Ad
cards.summary: A standard ad converts poorly unless the surrounding content is already about your product's category, so advertorials prime readers first.
cards.use_when: Deciding between a direct response ad and a sponsored-content placement, or sequencing top-of-funnel content before a product page for cold traffic.

cards.title: Actively Demonstrate the 70/30 Split (the Source's Exercise)
cards.summary: The source demonstrates building an advertorial by converting a bare 'product + Buy button' ad into a 70% value / 30% pitch piece.
cards.use_when: Workshopping or briefing a sponsored article draft for a product when your current creative is a flat product-plus-buy-button ad.

cards.title: Treat conversion rate as the primary growth lever when ad costs rise
cards.summary: Doubling conversion rate beats doubling traffic because CRO lifts ROI on every future dollar of ad spend and compounds.
cards.use_when: Deciding where to allocate budget and effort between paid traffic acquisition and landing page/checkout conversion work for your store.

cards.title: Run one split test per week and let wins compound
cards.summary: Testing one element per week forces focus and produces a compounding record of what your audience responds to.
cards.use_when: Setting up a repeatable landing page or PDP testing cadence for your store instead of ad-hoc redesigns.

cards.title: Use an A/B calculator to set test duration on low-traffic stores
cards.summary: Low-traffic stores should calculate required sample size before testing, or make sequential changes measured with session recordings instead.
cards.use_when: Planning how many tests your store can realistically run per month given its traffic and current conversion rate.

cards.title: Test the above-the-fold section first — it is the highest-leverage area
cards.summary: The top of the page is the only section 100% of visitors see and roughly 60% never scroll past it, so headline and hero image tests generate the largest gains.
cards.use_when: Choosing which page element to test next on a landing page, PDP, or homepage when you can only run one experiment.

cards.title: Write headlines that pass the 5-second who/what/benefit test
cards.summary: A headline must state who you are, what you do, and what's in it for the customer in under 5 seconds, with the benefit being the most important part.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing the main headline and subheadline on a store homepage, landing page, or product page.

cards.title: Use the 'so that' chain to find the deepest customer benefit
cards.summary: Repeatedly asking 'so that…' drills past the functional feature to the end outcome the customer actually wants.
cards.use_when: Developing headline, hero, or ad copy for your store when the first benefit you write sounds generic or feature-based.

cards.title: Map the Value Equation to specific page elements
cards.summary: Hormozi's four-part value framework becomes page components: dream outcome in the headline, perceived likelihood under the CTA, time delay in copy and shipping, effort in 'done-for-you' wording.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing product page or landing page to find which value component is missing or weak.

cards.title: De-risk the purchase with guarantees directly under the CTA
cards.summary: Placing trust badges, guarantees and return terms next to the buy button removes purchase uncertainty and, in the source's test, lifted conversion 30%.
cards.use_when: Optimizing a PDP or landing page where visitors hesitate or abandon near the add-to-cart or signup button.

cards.title: Quantify delivery and result timelines in copy and button labels
cards.summary: Reducing perceived time-to-result increases value; state shipping speed or result timelines in the copy and CTA, not just in policy pages.
cards.use_when: Writing PDP copy, shipping messaging, or CTA labels for a store where fulfillment speed or time-to-outcome is a purchase driver.

cards.title: Write 'done-for-you' copy to reduce perceived effort and sacrifice
cards.summary: Stating explicitly what the customer will not have to do lowers the effort component of value, especially for services and complex products.
cards.use_when: Writing hero or feature copy for a managed service, subscription, or product that replaces manual work your customer dislikes.

cards.title: Choose hero images that reinforce the value proposition
cards.summary: The hero image should visually demonstrate who you are and what you deliver; a weak or generic image is a common source of lost conversions.
cards.use_when: Selecting or testing the main image under the headline on a landing page, PDP, or homepage.

cards.title: Treat CRO results as transferable customer research, not just a page metric
cards.summary: Every winning or losing test reveals what resonates with your audience and can be redeployed across ads, positioning, and product decisions.
cards.use_when: Deciding what to do with test results beyond keeping or reverting the variant on your store's pages.

cards.title: Frame premium physical goods around status, not features
cards.summary: The dream outcome for a consumer product can be a felt status shift, which justifies a price far above the functional value of the materials.
cards.use_when: Positioning and pricing a premium or discretionary physical product in your store where competing on materials alone drives price comparisons.

cards.title: Always test the headline before any other page element
cards.summary: Headline tests produce the largest and most reliable gains, so make the headline the first and most frequent test on every page.
cards.use_when: Deciding the first experiment to run on a new or underperforming store page.

cards.title: Use product-quiz answers for recommendations and customer research
cards.summary: When building a store quiz that must select products and reveal buyer preferences.
cards.use_when: When building a store quiz that must select products and reveal buyer preferences.

cards.title: Place useful explanation screens between product-quiz questions
cards.summary: When shoppers abandon a quiz or cannot understand why a preference matters.
cards.use_when: When shoppers abandon a quiz or cannot understand why a preference matters.

cards.title: Choose quiz input controls that fit product decisions
cards.summary: When a product quiz repeats many identical button screens.
cards.use_when: When a product quiz repeats many identical button screens.

cards.title: Reflect product preferences in later quiz copy
cards.summary: When a recommendation quiz feels generic despite collecting useful answers.
cards.use_when: When a recommendation quiz feels generic despite collecting useful answers.

cards.title: Reveal the product-match explanation before the buy box
cards.summary: When shoppers need to understand why a quiz recommends a particular SKU or bundle.
cards.use_when: When shoppers need to understand why a quiz recommends a particular SKU or bundle.

cards.title: Use an occasion date to check product delivery suitability
cards.summary: When recommending products for gifts, travel, events or a move.
cards.use_when: When recommending products for gifts, travel, events or a move.

cards.title: Use routine and consumption to recommend a starter configuration
cards.summary: When a store must choose a product format, starter kit or replenishment interval.
cards.use_when: When a store must choose a product format, starter kit or replenishment interval.

cards.title: Keep the quiz result page focused on a transparent product offer
cards.summary: When quiz completion is strong but product purchases are weak.
cards.use_when: When quiz completion is strong but product purchases are weak.

cards.title: Targeted social proof matched to buying objections
cards.summary: Collect the top buying objections through surveys and user tests, then hand-pick testimonials that neutralize each objection and place them at the point of action.
cards.use_when: Placing reviews and testimonials on a PDP or landing page, or when generic featured-in logos and star ratings aren't moving add-to-cart rates.

cards.title: Let product imagery carry the value proposition
cards.summary: Because visitors skim text and process images far faster, build each PDP or landing page image set so the images alone communicate emotional, social and functional benefits.
cards.use_when: Replacing or briefing product photography, lifestyle imagery, and image galleries on a product page or landing page.

cards.title: Above-the-fold formula: value prop, visual, CTA, social proof
cards.summary: The above-the-fold area is the only section guaranteed to be seen, so it must answer 'what's in it for me', reinforce with a visual, show one obvious CTA, and stack trust immediately.
cards.use_when: Redesigning the top of a homepage, PDP or paid landing page, or auditing a page where the hero is vague or has competing buttons.

cards.title: Establish visual hierarchy with size and color contrast
cards.summary: Guide the eye down the page by making the headline 3-4x the body text, grouping content in sections, and reserving strong color contrast for the CTA.
cards.use_when: Fixing a page that looks chaotic, has a headline the same size as body copy, or where it is unclear what action to take.

cards.title: Smart pop-up timing instead of early interruption
cards.summary: Trigger pop-ups on behavior rather than on page load; exit intent, post-add-to-cart and scroll-depth triggers reach people who are already engaged.
cards.use_when: Deciding when an email-capture or discount pop-up should fire on a landing page, PDP or category page.

cards.title: Reduce choice to raise conversion and AOV
cards.summary: Cull navigation items and bundle options so fewer decisions are required; the source found fewer bundles increased both conversion rate and average order value.
cards.use_when: Simplifying a cluttered navigation, a product page with too many variants or pack sizes, or a bundle selector with five or more tiers.

cards.title: Structure bundles and use price anchoring to lift AOV
cards.summary: Bundle complementary products at a bulk discount, keep the original 'compare at' price visible as an anchor, and spell out dollar savings in the bundle headline.
cards.use_when: Designing bundle offers, subscription tiers, or add-on rows on a PDP to raise average order value.

cards.title: Middle option bias to steer buyers to the target tier
cards.summary: Shape the savings ladder so the middle bundle looks like the safest, best-value choice, which moves buyers off the cheapest tier without pushing them to overcommit.
cards.use_when: Setting the tier structure and savings copy for a three-tier bundle or subscription offer.

cards.title: Systematically reduce fear, uncertainty and doubt at action points
cards.summary: Place guarantees, security badges, shipping clarity and transparent pricing directly beneath critical actions such as the Add to Cart button.
cards.use_when: Auditing the cart, checkout and PDP action areas for reasons shoppers hesitate or abandon.

cards.title: Humanize the brand to build know-like-trust
cards.summary: People buy from brands they know, like and trust, so add team stories, behind-the-scenes content and customer success videos, and write in a conversational voice.
cards.use_when: Building the About page, brand story modules on the homepage or PDP, and voice-and-tone guidance for product copy.

cards.title: Make product content scannable with bullets, icons and subheadings
cards.summary: Since most visitors scan rather than read, convert dense description blocks into bullets, icons, subheadings and bolded highlights.
cards.use_when: Rewriting product descriptions, ingredient or spec sections, FAQ blocks and landing page body copy.

cards.title: Run CRO tests with PXL prioritization and two-week minimums
cards.summary: Landing pages are never finished, so prioritize hypotheses by impact versus effort and run single-variable tests long enough to reach significance.
cards.use_when: Setting up an A/B testing roadmap for a store or deciding which page experiment to run next.

cards.title: Landing page composition for conversion
cards.summary: Strip navigation, footers and links from campaign landing pages and lead with benefit-driven copy to reduce exit paths and raise lead conversion.
cards.use_when: Building or auditing a dedicated landing page for a paid campaign, email push or launch, where the goal is a single action rather than site browsing.

cards.title: Page load speed threshold: target under 2 seconds
cards.summary: The source advises keeping landing pages under 2 seconds load time, claiming conversion drops roughly 50% per additional second.
cards.use_when: Setting performance budgets for a landing page or diagnosing why a page converts poorly despite good copy and offer.
